families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

meaning: Each tie is a pointer that landed. Whether the paper and the Lean say the same thing is a reading.

rows.fidelity_note: The definition requires joint smoothness of velocity and pressure on the closed half-space in time, and the prescribed initial velocity. The equations are imposed at positive times.
rows.name: Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution

rows.fidelity_note: For each ν>0, the conclusion chooses smooth compactly supported solenoidal data and excludes every global smooth solution with one L²-energy bound valid for all t≥0.
rows.name: Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace

rows.fidelity_note: The conclusion chooses smooth solenoidal data of period one in each coordinate and excludes global smooth solutions with that velocity periodicity, for every ν>0. It places no periodicity requirement on the pressure.
rows.name: Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus

rows.fidelity_note: The premise asks for smooth velocity and pressure, a positive recurrence period, an orthogonal spatial twist and a common decay constant. Its remaining clauses impose the similarity equation, incompressibility, nonvanishing, decay through second spatial derivatives, and pressure-gradient decay.
rows.name: Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists

rows.fidelity_note: The passage correctly describes the stated implication: the profile premise includes the additional decay bounds and the conclusion excludes global smooth bounded-energy evolution. A chosen trajectory and the estimates (1.6) are absent from this conclusion.
rows.name: Breakdown.breakdown_on_space

rows.fidelity_note: The conclusion excludes a global smooth solution even when only its velocity is periodic; it gives no trajectory or estimates (1.7). The moving-frame reduction and uniqueness supply the comparison with the paper's periodic-pressure solution class.
rows.name: Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus

rows.fidelity_note: The hypothesis is existence of a nonzero recurrent distributional profile with uniform L⁶ and gradient L² bounds and square-integrable second derivatives over a period. This direct implication to whole-space breakdown is distinct from the paper's smooth-profile formulation.
rows.name: Breakdown.breakdown_on_space_of_weak

rows.fidelity_note: For an admissible nonzero recurrent mild orbit, any dense linear subspace and any ε>0, the statement chooses a mild trajectory on [0,1) with initial datum in that subspace within ε of the orbit. It also retains a positive exponent and a bound for the rescaled trajectory's distance from that same orbit.
rows.name: Breakdown.TransferHolds

rows.fidelity_note: The first assertion gives one finite upper bound for the recurrent orbit's norm, valid at every similarity time.
rows.name: Breakdown.OrbitBoundStatement

rows.fidelity_note: The second assertion gives one strictly positive lower bound at every similarity time, assuming the orthogonal recurrence commutes with the heat and nonlinear evolution.
rows.name: Breakdown.OrbitNormStatement
rows.plain: The orbit stays away from zero

rows.fidelity_note: The short-interval inverse retains a finite-dimensional correction space, a bounded map with values in the chosen dense data space, and a bounded right inverse on the recurrent pieces. These are the correction data referred to in the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.StepDataStatement

ties.name: Breakdown.certificate_orbit
ties.plain: Earlier certificate gives a weak profile

rows.fidelity_note: The earlier certificate implication concludes only existence of a weak recurrent profile. Its conclusion does not identify the chosen parameter or retain the closeness, symmetry and smoothness assertions of Theorem 7.1.
rows.name: Breakdown.certificate_orbit
rows.plain: Earlier certificate gives a weak profile

rows.fidelity_note: The extended certificate implication has the same existential weak-profile conclusion. The full parameter, prescribed symmetries and estimates (7.38) do not appear in that conclusion.
rows.name: Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit
rows.plain: A certificate gives a weak profile

rows.fidelity_note: This is the bordered linear inversion step: compact convection, the coercive bound and the symmetry properties give a unique solve with the imposed pin constraints.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedBorderedInvertibleHolds_of

rows.fidelity_note: This step obtains the uniform gradient bound used to keep the nonlinear correction in the prescribed set, using the energy-growth and product estimates.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedSupBoundHolds_of

rows.fidelity_note: For each admissible parameter, the correction map is a strict contraction in the norm combining the weighted correction size and the gradient supremum.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldContractsHolds_of

rows.fidelity_note: The fixed-parameter theorem gives a held solution and uniqueness of its forcing coordinate and multiplier within the prescribed bounded class.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldExistsUniqueHolds_of

ties.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHolds_of
ties.plain: Parameter where the total force vanishes

rows.fidelity_note: After existence, uniqueness, continuity and the boundary enclosures are available, the theorem chooses a parameter where the original and corrective multipliers sum to zero.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHolds_of
rows.plain: Parameter where the total force vanishes

rows.fidelity_note: The finite-dimensional zero theorem applies to the mixed box and ellipsoid through a compact convex fixed-point argument. Its proof supplies the stated finite-dimensional step.
rows.name: Breakdown.Held.testSetZero

rows.fidelity_note: When the two multiplier vectors sum to zero, the actuator sum cancels in the distributional equation for the corrected profile. The proof also establishes the integrability needed for the pressure-gradient pairing to vanish.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldWeakEquationHolds_of

rows.fidelity_note: At a fixed parameter the definition imposes the nonlinear equation, exact pin constraints, symmetry, correction-plus-multiplier size at most 2ε and gradient essential supremum at most M.
rows.name: Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.IsHeldSolution

rows.fidelity_note: For the given recurrent mild orbit, the statement supplies smooth velocity and pressure with its period and orthogonal twist. The velocity agrees almost everywhere in space with the given orbit at each time.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.SmoothFieldOfOrbit

rows.fidelity_note: The linked definition lists the fifteen cell-system assumptions under which our wrapper theorem holds; it states no conclusion itself. The conclusion described in the sentence is that of our separately compiled wrapper, which is not part of the authors' library shown here.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

ties.name: Breakdown.certificate_orbit_proved
ties.plain: Earlier certificate gives a weak profile

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem derives existence of a weak recurrent profile from the earlier certificate assumptions, supplying the analytic ingredients in its proof.
rows.name: Breakdown.certificate_orbit_proved
rows.plain: Earlier certificate gives a weak profile

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem derives existence of a weak recurrent profile from the extended certificate assumptions, including the finite-row and adjoint conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit_proved

rows.fidelity_note: This is the weak-to-mild step used in the route: it converts the recurrent distributional profile into an admissible mild orbit once its physical representation and pairing estimates are supplied.
rows.name: Breakdown.WeakProfile.weakOrbitOfParts_holds

rows.fidelity_note: A nonzero admissible recurrent mild orbit gives compactly supported smooth data for which no global smooth bounded-energy solution exists.
rows.name: Breakdown.WeakProfile.breakdownOnSpace_of_orbit

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem composes the weak-profile conversion with the whole-space breakdown argument.
rows.name: Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_weak

rows.fidelity_note: This is the whole-space nonexistence conclusion at the end of the displayed route, quantified over every positive viscosity.
rows.name: Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace

rows.fidelity_note: This step turns existence of a weak recurrent profile into existence of a smooth recurrent profile with the required spatial decay.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.periodicLerayProfileExists_of_weak

rows.fidelity_note: The smooth recurrent profile implies the periodic nonexistence conclusion for every positive viscosity.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_profile

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem composes the weak-to-smooth profile step with the torus breakdown argument.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.breakdownOnTorus_of_weak

rows.fidelity_note: This is the final periodic nonexistence conclusion, requiring periodic velocity and allowing any smooth pressure.
rows.name: Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem supplies smooth representatives of the given recurrent mild orbit, preserving its recurrence.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.smoothFieldOfOrbit_holds

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem establishes the Oseen integral equation for that orbit from the kernel and convolution estimates.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.integralEquationOfOrbit_holds
rows.plain: The orbit satisfies the Oseen equation

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem supplies velocity decay through second spatial derivatives and pressure-gradient decay for the smooth orbit through the integral equation and far-field estimates.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.farFieldDecay_holds

rows.fidelity_note: The linked definition supplies the fifteen assumptions on the seven groups of cell data. The implication from those assumptions to breakdown is a separate theorem.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: This link gives the whole-space nonexistence conclusion alone. It does not state the implication from the cell conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace

rows.fidelity_note: The present condition does require distinct component, time-frequency and azimuthal-order triples and the denominator (|m|+1/2)². A historical claim about which revision changed it needs the earlier revision as well.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded

rows.fidelity_note: The present cell inequalities allow a zero lower bound for the curl-Hessian coefficient while keeping the Hessian lower bound strictly positive. This confirms the current requirements; the passage's proposed identification of a historical patch is not established by this definition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafValues

rows.fidelity_note: The current active harmonics are those with a nonzero velocity, vorticity, strain or vorticity-gradient component somewhere in the cell. The definition alone does not establish the history of the change.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels
rows.plain: Model harmonics active in a cell

rows.fidelity_note: The linked condition lists the assumptions on cell data; it contains no stated implication from an empty mesh to zero multipliers. That conclusion requires the support and coercivity arguments cited in the surrounding discussion.

topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.
topics.name: The fractional extension

topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).
topics.name: The blow-up statements

topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).
topics.name: Passing to the torus

topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).
topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions

topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).
topics.name: Monodromy and the correction

topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).
topics.name: Recurrent profiles

topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).
topics.name: From certificate to profile

topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).
topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate

topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.
topics.name: Encoded cell data

topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).
topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane

topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).
topics.name: Cells, traces and tails

topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).
topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests

topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).
topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound

topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).
topics.name: Changing the profile

topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).
topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error

topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
topics.name: The offset and the certificate
